goal: Speeds up ECDSA and Schnorr signing by plugging Bitcoin Core's hardware-optimized SHA256 into libsecp256k1
Benefits wallets and PSBT signing, the hot path for signature generation
Also lays groundwork for decoupling ECC context management toward the kernel library
reviewability: Ready to review now: CI is clean, no rebase needed, no unresolved objections
agreement: Strong support with six concept ACKs and no objections raised (w0xlt, fjahr, sedited, ismaelsadeeq, theStack, hebasto)
Reviewers explicitly welcome the change with enthusiastic wording (sedited, ismaelsadeeq, theStack)

categories.name: kernel
why: P3 because it moves ECC_Context into the consensus library as groundwork, not a direct kernel API change
No external kernel consumer is affected yet, this just unblocks future decoupling work
Marginal impact today, value is mostly leverage for later kernel work

categories.name: utils
why: P2 because it delivers a measured performance win to a widely used cryptographic primitive
Benchmarks show ECDSASign 13% faster and SchnorrSign 7% faster on ARM64 SHA-NI hardware
Also cleans up global crypto-context ownership, though the change is internal plumbing rather than a user feature
